hook: I want AI coaching that managers trust enough to let it run

builtFor.context: Voiceops turns millions of calls into coaching for every rep. The hard design question, in your own words, is when the product should show, ask, coach or act.

opportunities.title: Coaching Review
opportunities.body: Managers review only what needs them, with evidence.

opportunities.title: Evidence in seconds
opportunities.body: The call moment, not the transcript.

opportunities.title: Earned autonomy
opportunities.body: Auto-send unlocked from what managers approved.

body: My work has been in products where people act on what a system flagged: transaction monitoring at Youverify, where analysts needed evidence before acting.
I design for data-heavy, high-stakes decisions and prototype in code with AI tools.

bring.title: Trust in automated systems
bring.body: Tools where people act on what a system flagged and know when to step in.

bring.title: Design systems
bring.body: A component library that cut developer onboarding by 45%.

bring.title: AI-assisted prototyping
bring.body: Working prototypes in code, like this one.

systemsGets: Someone who designs the states between AI and people (draft, needs review, sent, undone) as one system across reps, managers and leaders.

opportunity.title: Coaching Review
opportunity.problem: Managers can't review every note for hundreds of reps, but sending everything skips the trust coaching needs.
opportunity.solution: Review only low-confidence and sensitive notes with the call moment as evidence, and unlock auto-send per note type from approval history.

firstWeek.intro: My first week would focus on how managers and reps use Voiceops today, then turning one customer request into a clear design decision.

days.body: Meet the team in New York. Learn the roadmap and top customer requests.
Sit with managers and reps at a customer, watch coaching happen.
Agree on one decision to make, grounded in what we saw.
Prototype it and review with the CTO and engineers.
Share the decision, prototype and test plan.

ask: I'd love to be Voiceops' founding product designer.
